_schema.description: Per-module dtype overrides keyed by model variant and mesh shape. Modules without an override use the model-wide default dtype (bfloat16). The model variant key is the basename of the model path; mesh shape is the worker grid (rows x cols, e.g. 1x2 / 1x8). Within a model, lookup tries the exact mesh-shape key first, then 'default'. Module keys: shared_mlp, attention, experts, router, lm_head, embedding. Allowed dtype values: bf16, bfp8, fp32. A mesh-shape entry REPLACES 'default' rather than merging into it, so it must list every module it wants overridden. 'embedding' cannot be bfp8: the embedding weight is stored ROW_MAJOR and BFLOAT8_B requires TILE.

gemma-4-12B-it._comment_wh_bf16: Measured on a real WH T3K; the figures live in the commit that set each entry. single_tile_matmul_ckc raises the m<=32 projections to HiFi3 + fp32 dest-acc for every weight dtype, so these overrides stack on top of that rather than enabling it. Per-module contribution was established by walking all 8 (shared_mlp, attention, lm_head) combinations at 1x8: attention dominates, shared_mlp is secondary and not needed once attention is bf16, and lm_head is indistinguishable from noise despite being the 262144-vocab projection and the largest single weight read per decode step -- do not promote lm_head expecting accuracy. 1x8 therefore takes attention only. 1x2 has only 2x12 GB and cannot also take attention in bf16 (it does not allocate), so it takes shared_mlp + lm_head. 1x4 stays all-bfp8 and still gains from the accumulator alone. 'embedding' can never be bfp8 -- it is stored ROW_MAJOR and BFLOAT8_B requires TILE.
